items.stem: A public health nurse teaches a household about classic scabies. For each statement, select Accurate or Not accurate.

rows.text: Scabies is most commonly spread by direct, prolonged skin-to-skin contact with a person who has scabies
All household members and close contacts should be treated at the same time, even if they have no symptoms yet
Clothing, towels, and bedding used next to the skin should be washed in hot water or otherwise decontaminated as directed
Scabies mites live for months on furniture and clothing, so environmental cleaning is useless and only the index client needs treatment

rationales.R1: Accurate. CDC: human scabies most commonly spreads by direct, prolonged skin-to-skin contact. Merck: transmission involves close contact.
rationales.R2: Accurate. CDC: treat all household members and close contacts at the same time. Merck: empiric treatment of close contacts even if asymptomatic.
rationales.R3: Accurate. CDC: wash clothing/towels/bedding in hot water or dry-clean/seal items. Merck: environmental decontamination is a prevention strategy.
rationales.R4: Not accurate. Mites generally do not survive more than 2–3 days away from human skin (CDC); contacts need concurrent treatment (CDC; Merck).

items.stem: A client receiving chemotherapy has severe neutropenia. Which nursing actions support neutropenic (protective) precautions and infection risk reduction? Select all that apply.

options.text: Perform meticulous hand hygiene and uphold aseptic technique before client contact
Avoid fresh flowers in the room because of infection risk (e.g., Aspergillus)
Teach avoidance of fresh fruit and uncooked meats that may carry foodborne contaminants
Room the client with another client who has active influenza to 'boost immunity'
Ignore new fever because localized infection signs are always obvious in neutropenia
Ensure visitors/staff follow masking and other protective measures as ordered to reduce opportunistic exposure

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: meticulous hand hygiene and aseptic technique reduce nosocomial infection in neutropenia.
rationales.B: Correct. OpenStax neutropenic precautions: avoid fresh flowers (Aspergillus/chemical exposure risk).
rationales.C: Correct. OpenStax: avoid fresh fruit and uncooked meats to reduce foodborne contaminants.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Protective precautions aim to reduce pathogen exposure; placing with influenza increases risk.
rationales.E: Incorrect. Merck: focal infection signs may be muted in neutropenia, but fever is present in most serious infections and warrants immediate empiric antibiotics.
rationales.F: Correct. OpenStax: providers, staff, and visitors wear masks to protect the patient from opportunistic infections.

items.stem: After a critical resuscitation, the charge nurse wants a short TeamSTEPPS after-action review focused on learning. Which action best matches a debrief?

options.text: Facilitate a brief end-of-event discussion (often initiated by the leader) that reviews what went well and what to improve, reinforces successful behaviours, and captures lessons for the next plan—without assigning individual blame.
Skip any review so the team never discusses performance.
Publicly shame one team member for any perceived mistake.
Wait until the next annual performance appraisal to discuss the event for the first time.

rationales.A: Correct. AHRQ: debriefs recount/analyze events, discuss lessons, reinforce what went well, avoid blame; often short and leader-facilitated. OpenStax: TeamSTEPPS debrief checklist at the end for reflection and continuous improvement.
rationales.B: Incorrect. TeamSTEPPS advocates after-action debriefs after critical team events (AHRQ).
rationales.C: Incorrect. AHRQ: avoid assigning blame; focus on performance improvement and learning.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Debriefs are timely after events (AHRQ), not deferred to annual appraisal only.

items.stem: A pregnant client in the first trimester has persistent severe vomiting with signs of significant dehydration, ketosis, and weight loss. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.text: This presentation is consistent with hyperemesis gravidarum and may require hospitalization for fluid and electrolyte replacement and further management.
Severe vomiting with dehydration and weight loss in early pregnancy is always harmless 'morning sickness' that never needs evaluation.
All first-trimester nausea requires immediate chemotherapy.
Weight loss and ketosis prove the client should stop all prenatal care.

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: hyperemesis gravidarum is persistent severe pregnancy-induced vomiting causing significant dehydration, often with electrolyte abnormalities, ketosis, and weight loss. OpenStax: severe nausea/vomiting with electrolyte imbalance, weight loss, malnutrition, and dehydration may require hospitalization for fluid/electrolyte replacement.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Ordinary nausea/vomiting of pregnancy is common; hyperemesis is the severe form needing evaluation/possible hospital care (Merck; OpenStax).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Not the treatment pathway described for hyperemesis in these sources.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Clients need supportive care and prenatal follow-up, not cessation of care.

items.stem: Complete the teaching for a pregnant client about HELLP syndrome associated with severe preeclampsia.

ngn.template: HELLP stands for {B1}, elevated liver enzymes, and {B2}. It can develop in some clients with severe preeclampsia/eclampsia and requires {B3}.

B3.text: prompt evaluation and close monitoring because it can be life-threatening to the pregnant person and fetus
no follow-up because HELLP is always harmless
routine delayed outpatient labs in 6 months only

rationales.B1a: Correct. Merck and OpenStax: H = hemolysis in HELLP.
rationales.B1b: Incorrect. Hypercalcemia is not the H in HELLP.
rationales.B1c: Incorrect. Hyponatremia is not the defining H component.
rationales.B1d: Incorrect. HELLP involves hemolysis, not high hemoglobin as the acronym letter.
rationales.B2b: Incorrect. Platelets are low, not elevated.
rationales.B2c: Incorrect. Low bilirubin alone is not the LP component.
rationales.B2d: Incorrect. Not the LP meaning in HELLP.
rationales.B3a: Correct. OpenStax: HELLP can be life-threatening; close monitoring and prompt evaluation are necessary. Merck: HELLP develops in a subset with severe preeclampsia/eclampsia.
rationales.B3b: Incorrect. HELLP is a serious complication.
rationales.B3c: Incorrect. Prompt evaluation is required, not remote delayed labs only.
rationales.B3d: Incorrect. Not evidence-based management from cited sources.

items.stem: A breastfeeding client on postpartum day 4 has firm, swollen, painful breasts with a flattened nipple that makes latch difficult. Which teaching is most appropriate?

options.text: Use warm compress or a warm shower and hand-express a small amount of milk to soften the breast and help the nipple protrude for latch; continue frequent feeding; cool compresses between feedings may reduce inflammation.
Stop breastfeeding permanently at the first sign of engorgement.
Avoid any feeding or expression so milk pressure rises indefinitely.
Apply ice packs continuously for 24 hours without feeding the infant.

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: warm compress/shower and hand expression to soften for latch; cool compress between feedings. Merck: expressing milk (warm shower/pump) temporarily for pressure relief and breastfeeding on a regular schedule for those who will breastfeed.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Engorgement is managed while continuing lactation support for breastfeeding clients (both sources).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Regular feeding/appropriate expression relieves engorgement (Merck; OpenStax).
rationales.D: Incorrect. Continuous icing without feeding is not the cited breastfeeding engorgement plan; cool packs are adjunct between feeds (OpenStax).

items.stem: A nurse teaches expected postpartum lochia changes. For each statement, select Accurate or Not accurate.

rows.text: Lochia rubra is grossly bloody/red discharge expected in the first few postpartum days
Lochia then typically becomes pale brown (serosa) and later yellowish white (alba)
Saturating a peripad in less than 1 hour is considered excessive and needs prompt uterine assessment
Foul-smelling discharge is expected normal lochia and never needs clinician contact

rationales.R1: Accurate. Merck: lochia rubra grossly bloody for ~3–4 days. OpenStax: lochia rubra bright/dark red for about the first 1–4 days.
rationales.R2: Accurate. Merck: pale brown (serosa) then yellowish white (alba). OpenStax describes progression of lochia types with assessment teaching.
rationales.R3: Accurate. OpenStax: saturating a pad in <1 hour is excessive and requires immediate uterine assessment. Merck advises contacting clinician for concern about heavy bleeding.
rationales.R4: Not accurate. OpenStax: foul odor may signal uterine infection—contact the provider.

items.stem: Which nursing strategies help prevent or reduce hospital delirium risk in an older adult? Select all that apply.

options.text: Maintain orientation with cues (e.g., date/time, staff names, visual reminders) and involve family for familiarity when appropriate
Promote sleep hygiene and protect rest when possible
Support mobility/assistance with movement and address pain, nutrition, and hydration
Add as many new psychoactive medications as possible without review
Keep the same caregivers as much as possible to reduce confusion
Leave sensory aids (glasses/hearing devices) unavailable all admission so the client 'adjusts'

rationales.A: Correct. Merck prevention: maintain orientation; family can help. OpenStax: whiteboards/cues and family familiarity.
rationales.B: Correct. Merck: ensure sleep. OpenStax: promote sleep hygiene.
rationales.C: Correct. Merck: mobility, nutrition, hydration, pain relief. OpenStax: assist with movement; treat pain; proper nutrition.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Merck: reduce number/doses of medications if possible; new meds can precipitate delirium.
rationales.E: Correct. OpenStax: keep the same caregivers as much as possible.
rationales.F: Incorrect. Sensory impairment predisposes to delirium (Merck); aids should be available, not withheld.

items.stem: A nurse educates a client with asthma and the caregiver about self-management. Which teaching point is most strongly supported?

options.text: Provide a written asthma action plan describing day-to-day management and what to do for exacerbations (often guided by the client's best personal peak flow), plus inhaler/spacer technique and trigger awareness.
Tell the client never to have any written plan because asthma cannot be self-monitored.
Advise using peak-flow–based decisions only against a stranger's predicted normal value and never the client's personal best.
Recommend waiting until severe respiratory failure before any early glucocorticoid use discussed in an action plan.

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: every patient should have a written action plan for daily and acute management based on best personal peak flow; education includes triggers and inhaler/spacer technique. OpenStax: implement an asthma action plan to monitor symptoms and adjust medications; written personalized plans help caregivers/patients stay safe.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Written action plans improve control/adherence (Merck; OpenStax).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Merck emphasizes the patient's best personal peak flow rather than predicted normal alone.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Merck notes importance of early glucocorticoid use in exacerbations as part of education.

items.stem: A nurse cares for a large-for-gestational-age newborn of a mother with diabetes. Which priority approach is most appropriate regarding neonatal hypoglycemia risk?

options.text: Follow facility protocol for glucose monitoring of at-risk newborns, support early feeding (often within the first hour), and treat confirmed hypoglycemia with enteral feeding or IV dextrose as ordered—do not wait for seizures before acting.
Never monitor glucose in infants of diabetic mothers because hypoglycemia never occurs in this group.
Withhold all feeds for 12 hours to 'test' hypoglycemia tolerance.
Treat only with adult oral hypoglycemic tablets crushed into formula.

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: risk factors include maternal diabetes; treatment is enteral feeding or IV dextrose; signs can include seizures/apnea. OpenStax: IDM/LGA are at risk; monitor at-risk newborns per policy; encourage early breastfeeding; prevent cold stress; do not wait for all term newborns to become symptomatic before protocol monitoring.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Infants of diabetic mothers are a classic risk group (Merck; OpenStax).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Early feeding is preventive/supportive (OpenStax; Merck treatment includes feeding).
rationales.D: Incorrect. Not the neonatal pathway in cited sources (feeding/IV dextrose).

items.stem: A client with chemotherapy-related severe neutropenia develops a new fever. Complete the bowtie: identify the priority condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.

conditions.text: Febrile neutropenia / presumed serious infection due to severe neutropenia
Uncomplicated seasonal allergies without infection risk

actions.text: Notify the provider and initiate ordered empiric high-dose broad-spectrum IV antibiotics promptly
Delay all antibiotics for 48 hours to 'see if fever resolves alone'
Obtain ordered cultures and implement protective/neutropenic precautions (hand hygiene, limit exposure)
Send the client to a crowded public event without masking
Stop temperature monitoring for the shift

parameters.text: Absolute neutrophil count and signs of clinical instability (e.g., hypotension)

rationales.K1: Correct. Merck: with fever in neutropenia, infection is presumed and immediate empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics are necessary.
rationales.K2: Incorrect. Not the acute life-threatening problem described.
rationales.K3: Incorrect. Does not explain febrile neutropenia urgency.
rationales.A1: Correct. Merck: immediate empiric high-dose broad-spectrum IV antibiotics when fever/hypotension present.
rationales.A2: Incorrect. Delaying antibiotics is unsafe in febrile neutropenia (Merck).
rationales.A3: Correct. Cultures are part of infection evaluation; OpenStax emphasizes protective precautions and infection surveillance.
rationales.A5: Incorrect. OpenStax: routine temperature surveillance is essential.
rationales.P1: Correct. Fever drives urgent treatment decisions (Merck); OpenStax monitors temperature.
rationales.P2: Correct. Neutrophil count severity and hypotension guide urgency (Merck); OpenStax monitors ANC and infection signs.
rationales.P3: Incorrect. Not a clinical parameter for this emergency.

items.stem: Which finding best aligns with the definition of preeclampsia used in standard clinical references?

options.text: New-onset (or worsening) hypertension with proteinuria after 20 weeks' gestation (with evaluation for end-organ involvement as indicated)
Isolated mild headache at 8 weeks with normal blood pressure and no proteinuria
Chronic hypertension diagnosed years before pregnancy with no change after 20 weeks and no proteinuria
Postprandial fullness in the second trimester without hypertension

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: preeclampsia is new onset or worsening hypertension with proteinuria after 20 weeks, with evaluation for end-organ damage. OpenStax covers hypertensive disorders of pregnancy including preeclampsia after mid-pregnancy with monitoring/management implications.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Too early and lacks hypertension/proteinuria criteria (Merck: after 20 weeks).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Pre-existing chronic hypertension without new features is a different category (OpenStax/Merck distinguish hypertensive disorders).
